findings.statement: The alpha store holds local run metadata for sub-1 MB runs and must provide run-ID lookup, latest-100 listing, portable inspection/export, and safe near-simultaneous completion on macOS and Linux.

Append-only JSONL is the smaller alpha architecture because the bounded access patterns tolerate scanning while line-oriented data remains directly inspectable and schema changes can be represented per record.
Without process-level serialization and a single complete-record append, two finishing processes could interleave or leave a partial final record, corrupting subsequent reads.
Appending before contract validation or field allowlisting could permanently retain malformed metadata, raw prompts, or secrets in an otherwise immutable history.
As history grows, exact lookup and latest-100 listing remain linear scans and may eventually become too slow or memory-intensive for the CLI experience.

The alpha design should validate and redact an allowlisted record before taking an inter-process lock, append exactly one newline-delimited record, flush it durably, and make readers reject or explicitly report malformed trailing data.

Migrate the canonical store to SQLite when measured history scans or file-level writer serialization fail an explicit supported latency or concurrency target; SQLite then supplies indexed lookup and transactional multi-process writes.

No expected lifetime run count, latency target, crash-consistency test result, filesystem behavior, or accountable action owner is provided, so the controls and migration threshold require validation before release.

alternatives: Use SQLite immediately for transactional concurrency and indexed queries, accepting migration management and less direct canonical-file inspection during a schema-volatile alpha.

method_artifact.system_boundary: Local CLI run-metadata history only; artifact payload storage, raw prompts, secrets, server sync, and implementation are excluded.
failure_modes: reader fails on malformed trailing record
schema-version drift makes old records unreadable
effects: run history becomes incomplete or ambiguous
lookup/listing returns incorrect or unavailable results
sensitive content remains in append-only history
CLI responsiveness degrades as history grows
propagation_paths: write failure -> malformed record -> reader/export failure
missing validation -> persisted sensitive field -> disclosure through inspection/export
history growth -> repeated full scan -> lookup/list latency
detections: schema validation before append and during read
lookup/list latency measurement over representative history
controls: allowlist persisted metadata and exclude raw prompts and secrets
hold an inter-process lock for one complete newline-delimited append
flush completed writes and never silently skip malformed records
version each record and retain backward-compatible readers or explicit migration
actions: Before release, the storage maintainer must define latency and concurrency targets and verify concurrent, interrupted, malformed, and schema-evolution cases.
Adopt append-only JSONL for alpha and retain export as a stable user-facing capability.
Move to SQLite when measured scans or writer serialization breach the defined target.
limitations: Preliminary qualitative review based on one architecture fixture
No implementation, benchmarks, crash tests, filesystem tests, or domain-expert review
No common-cause step or numerical risk assessment at standard rigor
unknowns: filesystem and lock behavior across supported deployments
named human owner for release verification

confidence.basis: The choice fits the stated alpha scale and portability goals, but concurrency and growth controls lack measured validation.

change_conditions: Choose SQLite instead when measured full-history scans or serialized append contention breach an explicit supported latency or concurrency target.
